clue.text: Take it from chum — our lesson's not funny

indicators.note: the solver is told to lift the word straight out of the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters run on across the words after the C of chum and before the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A pupil grumbles to a friend that today's lesson was a joyless slog.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and apostrophe are ignored; the hidden run spans three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something humourless lacks any comedy, so it is plainly not funny.

clue.text: Pay attention to four-letter word included by the editor

indicators.note: the wanted word is held inside the following words, sitting across their join

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An editor is warned about a swear word slipping into print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests something rude, but it simply announces the length of the word hidden in 'the editor'.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed someone is to listen and take notice of what they say, a direct synonym.

clue.text: French officer post-war planner listened to or cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its tail, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: George Marshall, the US statesman behind the Marshall Plan for rebuilding Europe after 1945
surface padding offering an alternative route: the planner's name heard aloud already matches the answer

explanation.surface: A historian describes a military man and an American planner after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listened to or' offers a second route: the name heard aloud is the same as the answer. Either way the double L becomes one.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshal of France is the highest military rank in the French army, so a French officer.

clue.text: Covered by and contained within smart agreement

indicators.note: something contained within another sits inside it, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: to be covered by something is to be under it
to smart is to sting with pain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neat deal is said to be both covered by and held within a clever agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An understanding is an informal arrangement between parties, so another word for agreement.

clue.text: Awkwardly move unwanted furniture etc

blocks.note: first meaning: to walk heavily and clumsily
second meaning: British for disused household items stored away

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to shift old furniture nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage lumber is junk such as old furniture kept in a lumber room, not just timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes a heavy clumsy gait, and the British noun names discarded household clutter.

clue.text: Namely, object about note that's extremely critical

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer pieces wrap the note

blocks.note: abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely
an object is a thing
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A reviewer's note on some object is described as harshly critical.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the dictionary abbreviation for scilicet, 'namely'; the note slips in between it and the object.
explanation.definitionFit: A scathing remark is bitterly severe and wounding, so extremely critical.

clue.text: Identify bird in swamp, initially, as wader

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the run

blocks.note: the leading letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is told to spot a bird standing in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged, curved-billed bird that feeds in shallow water, so a wader.

clue.text: Aristocrat, with a single exception, is on time

blocks.note: 'bar one' means except for one
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: All the nobility are punctual, apart from one.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron, so a minor aristocrat.

clue.text: Thus illuminated sign for people living alone

blocks.note: so means thus
illuminated means lit up
a sign of the zodiac, the ram

explanation.surface: A lit-up sign seems to advertise for single people.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary is a recluse or hermit, so solitaries are people who live on their own.

clue.text: Title that could make me a lord

indicators.note: these words say the letters could be made into something else by rearranging

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone hopes an honour will turn them into a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is neatly apt: an earldom really would make you a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank and title held by an earl, a British peerage.

clue.text: Endlessly respect everyone, being top man on board

indicators.note: endlessly says each word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to respect someone is to admire them
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A captain earns respect from the whole crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means aboard a ship: an admiral commands a fleet from a flagship.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking naval officer, so the senior figure aboard a navy ship.

clue.text: Captain being careful and expertly steering

blocks.note: the master is the captain of a merchant ship
minding as in 'mind the step', taking care

explanation.surface: A ship's captain steers with care and skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To mastermind a scheme is to plan and direct it cleverly, so expertly steering it.

clue.text: Disturbed thrushes etc, on tree

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Songbirds and others are startled while perched on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a large tree known for its conkers, the shiny seeds children play with.

clue.text: Expressed regret in article composed about record

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the indefinite article
composed means calm and poised
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Someone said sorry in a carefully written piece about a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say sorry, which is to express regret for something done.

clue.text: Sense of taste revealed as friend dined

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A companion's discernment in food shows when the pair eat together.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the roof of the mouth and, by extension, a person's ability to judge flavour.

clue.text: Would-be moneymaker having chest covered with gold

blocks.note: someone whose chest is covered is wearing a vest: 'in vest'
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A wealth-seeker shows off a gold-draped torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' looks like a treasure chest full of gold, but it is the body; a vest covers it.
explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts money into ventures hoping for a return, so someone aiming to profit.

clue.text: American round the bend and out of sight

indicators.note: round the bend means crazy, and crazy letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A US driver turns a corner and disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, hidden from the public.

clue.text: Second in class, deserving scholarship

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the next word

blocks.note: the letter after the C
earning as in deserving praise

explanation.surface: A pupil ranked second in the class merits a scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scholarship' looks like a grant, but here it means scholarly knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning means acquired knowledge and erudition, which is scholarship in its academic sense.

clue.text: A sinner's behaviour, including extremes of anger or greed

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the outermost letters are wanted
including means holding inside, so the selected letters go within

blocks.note: taken as written
a vice is wicked conduct
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Sinful conduct, here framed in terms of the deadly sins of wrath or covetousness.
explanation.walkthrough: Anger and greed are both deadly sins, so 'or' reads as part of the list but is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, a synonym for greed and one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Child liable to be beaten with stout stick

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child, the sort once likely to get a beating
stout is a dark beer, so a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A naughty youngster faces a thrashing with a thick cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout stick' reads as a cudgel, but stout is the beer and stick is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce or stick something through with a sharp point.

clue.text: Menial poorly, with temperature — contracted illness

indicators.note: poorly means badly or unwell, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: the fodder letters
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A lowly servant is unwell, running a fever after catching something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor sickness or disorder, so a synonym for illness.

clue.text: Bird left, trapped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
something trapped is 'in net'

explanation.surface: A bird remains caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch once popular as a cage bird.

clue.text: Kind of field changed to a vital grain

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A farmer converts a meadow to growing an essential cereal crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' suggests farmland, which the grain supports, but it is the physics sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravitational field is the region of force around a mass, so one kind of physics field.

clue.text: The speaker had briefly spoken and made observations

indicators.note: spoken tells the solver to go by how the words are said, not spelt

blocks.note: the speaker is I, and 'I had' contracted is I'd

explanation.surface: Someone had spoken briefly and then watched.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyed means watched or made observations.

clue.text: Outside hospital, unattached piece of roof

indicators.note: outside places one word around the other, so the hospital letter sits within

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
someone unattached is single

explanation.surface: A loose roof tile has fallen outside a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle is a thin wooden or slate tile laid in overlapping rows to cover a roof.

clue.text: Unusually vain, yet showing lack of sophistication

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A conceited person who still seems surprisingly unworldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence and inexperience of the world, so a want of sophistication.

clue.text: Decrease in eating through only taking starters?

definitions.text: Decrease in eating through only taking starters?

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the leading letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back on food by ordering just the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition words also form part of the fodder, and 'starters' doubles as the restaurant course.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on a diet means restricting food intake, a reduction in how much one eats.

clue.text: Group seen playing I kept in and reprimanded

blocks.note: the cast are the actors seen in a play
taken as written
a gated pupil is confined to school as punishment

explanation.surface: A child explains that the band were performing while they were kept at home and scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: Gated is British school slang for being confined to the premises as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke someone severely, so castigated means sharply reprimanded.
